translation:
Heat-pathogen consuming water becomes thirst; heat-pathogen gathering at the mouth makes the mouth dry. A cup of water can hardly save a cartload of burning firewood; the exhaustion and evaporation of fluids, why is it trivial?
The tongue is the sprout of the heart; its color is naturally red. White fur, yellow and smooth, hard and without markings; most to be feared is kidney water (cold) overwhelming heart fire, the tongue growing blood thorns and the pulse being especially surging.
translator_notes: 舌乃心苗=the tongue is the sprouting shoot of the heart.
腎水克心火=kidney water overcoming heart fire.
unresolved: "舌胎"=tongue coating (fúr); 強無紋 obscure — rendered literally.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Nosebleed's root cause is heat pressing the blood; running wantonly in the nose, the body sweats blocked. The Classics say one who dashes out blood has no sweat; in the method of treatment, make sweat rush and there will be no bleeding.
If all seven orifices flow blood together, take the cold damage red-sweat as the standard. Hematemesis with intense heat, do not doubt; leading the blood back to its channels is truly one attainment.
translator_notes: 紅汗=red sweat (nose bleed as a way of resolving exterior heat).
引血歸經=sending the blood back to its channels.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
As to its origin, the spasm (zhi) condition belongs to the bladder; head, neck stiff and straight, the back arched backward. This is wind damage contracting damp-cold; the ancestral sinews pulling cause the contraction and cramping.
Eyes open and no sweat: hard spasm (gang zhi); belonging to yin, body hot — Gegen Tang (Kudzu Root Decoction). Eyes closed and sweating: soft spasm (rou zhi); belonging to yin, cold limbs — Guizhi Tang (Cinnamon Twig Decoction).
The condition of flaccid-spasm (chizhong) has heat engendering wind; wind pathogen being active gives rise to flying chaos. Chi (瘈) is to contract and tighten, zhong (瘲) to extend and loosen; supplement blood and nourish sinews, the medicine carries warmth.
Fighting and shivering (zhan-su), yin and yang fight each other; Heaven and Earth rock and sway without life. When the pathogen and proper qi contend, that is zhan (shivering in struggle); su (憟) is the pathogen qi fighting and rushing within.
Flesh twitching and sinew throbbing (rou shun jin ti) are not frequent occurrences; ti (惕) is moving, shun (瞤) is jumping. When fluids are passed and blood dries and withers, sinew and flesh lose nourishment; nourishing them is excellent.
translator_notes: 痓=zhi spasm; 剛痓=hard spasm; 柔痓=soft spasm.
瘈瘲=chìzòng (spasm with contraction/relaxation); 戰憟=shivering.
葛根湯=Gegen Tang; 桂枝湯=Guizhi Tang.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
